content:
You are visiting San Francisco for the day and want to meet as many friends as possible. Solve the problem by considering various different schedules and picking the best one to optimize your goals.

Travel distances (in minutes):
Pacific Heights to North Beach: 9.
Pacific Heights to Financial District: 13.
Pacific Heights to Alamo Square: 10.
Pacific Heights to Mission District: 15.
North Beach to Pacific Heights: 8.
North Beach to Financial District: 8.
North Beach to Alamo Square: 16.
North Beach to Mission District: 18.
Financial District to Pacific Heights: 13.
Financial District to North Beach: 7.
Financial District to Alamo Square: 17.
Financial District to Mission District: 17.
Alamo Square to Pacific Heights: 10.
Alamo Square to North Beach: 15.
Alamo Square to Financial District: 17.
Alamo Square to Mission District: 10.
Mission District to Pacific Heights: 16.
Mission District to North Beach: 17.
Mission District to Financial District: 17.
Mission District to Alamo Square: 11.

CONSTRAINTS: You arrive at Pacific Heights at 9:00AM. Helen will be at North Beach from 9:00AM to 5:00PM. You'd like to meet Helen for a minimum of 15 minutes. Betty will be at Financial District from 7:00PM to 9:45PM. You'd like to meet Betty for a minimum of 90 minutes. Amanda will be at Alamo Square from 7:45PM to 9:00PM. You'd like to meet Amanda for a minimum of 60 minutes. Kevin will be at Mission District from 10:45AM to 2:45PM. You'd like to meet Kevin for a minimum of 45 minutes.

Your response should start with 'SOLUTION:'.

Please output the meeting schedule in the following JSON format:
{"itinerary": [{"action": "meet", "person": "<PERSON_NAME>", "start_time": "<HH:MM>", "end_time": "<HH:MM>"}]}. Make sure to include the person's name for each meeting.

SOLUTION:
After analyzing various alternatives it turns out that the evening “window” makes it impossible to meet both Amanda (at Alamo Square, available 7:45–9:00 for a 60‐minute chat) and Betty (at the Financial District, available 7:00–9:45 for a 90‐minute chat) in one day when including the necessary travel time. In other words, with all travel times taken into account you can “fit” meetings with your morning friends (Helen and Kevin) plus one of the two evening friends. That is, the maximum number of friends you can meet while satisfying all minimum meeting durations is three.

One good optimized schedule is as follows:

1. Start at Pacific Heights at 09:00.
 • Travel from Pacific Heights to North Beach (9 minutes) so you arrive by about 09:09.
2. Meet Helen at North Beach from 09:09 to 09:24 (15 minutes minimum, and her window is 09:00–17:00).
 • Then leave North Beach at 09:24 and travel 18 minutes to Mission District (arriving ≈09:42).
3. Wait until Kevin’s availability begins at 10:45. Then meet Kevin at Mission District from 10:45 to 11:30 (45 minutes, his window is 10:45–14:45).
4. (After a long afternoon gap you reposition for your evening meeting.)
 • To maximize the number of friends you get a full meeting, choose Betty in the evening. (Because if you attempt to “split” time between Betty and Amanda the required travel gaps force the total meeting duration with one of them below the minimum.) 
 • Travel (at your leisure later in the day) so you are in the Financial District by 19:00.
 • Meet Betty in the Financial District from 19:00 to 20:30 (90 minutes, fitting within her 19:00–21:45 availability).

This schedule meets the minimum meeting requirements for Helen, Kevin, and Betty. (An alternate valid schedule would be to meet Amanda in the evening from, say, 19:45 to 20:45, but then you would have met only three friends as well.) 

Below is the itinerary in the required JSON format:

{
  "itinerary": [
    {
      "action": "meet",
      "person": "Helen",
      "start_time": "09:09",
      "end_time": "09:24"
    },
    {
      "action": "meet",
      "person": "Kevin",
      "start_time": "10:45",
      "end_time": "11:30"
    },
    {
      "action": "meet",
      "person": "Betty",
      "start_time": "19:00",
      "end_time": "20:30"
    }
  ]
}

This plan optimizes your goals by meeting three friends—two in the morning with ample travel time and one evening visit—since it is not possible (given travel and time-window constraints) to pack in both evening meetings while satisfying everyone’s minimum meeting durations.
